summary: Small hexagonal service: an HTTP adapter (Spring MVC @RestController) over a storage port (LinkStore) with an in-memory adapter, and a pure code-generation class. The controller owns validation and status codes; the store owns links and click counters; Codes owns randomness. Tests boot the real context on a random port and use java.net.http.

components.name: LinkController
components.responsibility: Routes, URL policy, 302/no-store redirects, JSON responses.

components.name: LinkStore port + InMemory adapter
components.responsibility: Persist links and click counters; the seam for a JDBC adapter.

components.name: Codes
components.responsibility: Random base62 codes with rejection sampling; bounded collision retry.

dataFlow: POST /api/links -> validateUrl (http/https only) -> Codes.unique(store::exists) -> store.insert -> 201 {code, shortUrl, targetUrl, createdAt}

decisions.decision: Random base62 codes (7 chars) instead of an encoded counter.
decisions.rationale: Counters are enumerable; random codes with a collision check are not. 62^7 ≈ 3.5e12 keys.
decisions.tradeoffs: Needs an existence check per create; negligible at v0 scale.

decisions.rationale: 301 is cached by browsers, which would hide repeat clicks from analytics.
decisions.tradeoffs: Slightly more traffic to the service; acceptable, analytics is a requirement.

decisions.decision: Storage behind a LinkStore port with an in-memory adapter.
decisions.rationale: Zero-setup local run now; JDBC/Postgres later without touching the controller.
decisions.tradeoffs: Data lost on restart in v0 (documented).

decisions.decision: Validate URLs explicitly in the controller with a scheme allowlist.
decisions.rationale: javascript:/data: targets would make the redirect an XSS vector.

securityConsiderations: Path templates constrain codes to 7 base62 characters
No user input is reflected in responses unescaped
rollbackStrategy: v0 is a new service: rollback is stopping the process. No data migration exists.
